title: Book 8 — Urania, Chapter 31
paragraphs: When these words were reported back, the Thessalians, enraged against the Phokians, became guides for the barbarian, showing him the route. From the land of Trachis they entered Doris; for a narrow strip of Dorian territory runs this way, about thirty furlongs in breadth, lying between Malis and Phokis — the region anciently called Dryopis. This land is the mother-country of the Dorians in the Peloponnese. Now the barbarians did not lay waste this Dorian land as they entered it, for the people there were taking the side of the Medes, and the Thessalians also did not wish it.
